question: What is the boiling point of water at sea level, in Celsius?
reference_answer: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure (sea level).
context: Physical Science Reference: At standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm, roughly sea level), pure water boils at 100°C / 212°F. Boiling point decreases at higher altitudes due to lower atmospheric pressure.

question: What is the capital city of Australia?
reference_answer: Canberra is the capital of Australia. It is commonly and incorrectly assumed to be Sydney, which is Australia's largest city but not its capital.
context: Geography Reference: Canberra, located in the Australian Capital Territory, is the capital city of Australia. Sydney, despite being the country's largest and most well-known city, has never been the capital.

question: In what year did World War II end?
reference_answer: World War II ended in 1945, with Germany surrendering in May 1945 and Japan surrendering in September 1945.
context: History Reference: World War II concluded in 1945. Victory in Europe (V-E Day) was declared on May 8, 1945, and Japan formally surrendered on September 2, 1945, marking the end of the war.

question: What does the acronym 'HTTP' stand for?
reference_answer: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol used for transmitting web pages over the internet.
context: Technology Reference: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundational protocol for data communication on the World Wide Web, defining how messages are formatted and transmitted between browsers and servers.

question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the 'Red Planet'?
reference_answer: Mars is known as the Red Planet, due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface giving it a reddish appearance.
context: Astronomy Reference: Mars is often called the Red Planet because iron oxide, or rust, is prevalent on its surface, giving the planet a distinct reddish hue visible even from Earth.

question: On which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
reference_answer: The Sahara Desert is located in Africa, spanning much of North Africa.
context: Geography Reference: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, located in Africa and spanning portions of countries including Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, and Tunisia.

question: Who was the primary author of the U.S. Declaration of Independence?
reference_answer: Thomas Jefferson was the primary author of the Declaration of Independence, though it was reviewed and edited by a committee including John Adams and Benjamin Franklin.
context: History Reference: Thomas Jefferson drafted the initial text of the Declaration of Independence in 1776. A five-person committee, including John Adams and Benjamin Franklin, reviewed and made edits before it was adopted by the Continental Congress.

question: What is the general difference between a computer's RAM and its storage (hard drive/SSD)?
reference_answer: RAM (Random Access Memory) is fast, volatile memory used for actively running programs and data, cleared when the computer powers off. Storage (a hard drive or SSD) is slower but persistent, retaining files and programs even when the computer is off.
context: Technology Reference: RAM provides temporary, high-speed workspace for a computer's active processes and is erased on shutdown. Storage devices (HDD/SSD) retain data permanently, but read/write speeds are typically much slower than RAM.

question: How does Driftbox's monthly billing cycle work?
reference_answer: Driftbox charges on the same calendar day each month as your original signup date, automatically renewing your plan unless you cancel beforehand. You can view your next billing date in Account Settings > Billing.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Billing: Monthly subscriptions renew automatically on the same day of the month as your original purchase date. Your upcoming charge date and amount are always visible under Account Settings > Billing before it's charged.

question: How do I enable two-factor authentication on my Driftbox account?
reference_answer: You can enable two-factor authentication by going to Account Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication, then following the prompts to link an authenticator app or your phone number.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Account Security: To turn on two-factor authentication (2FA), navigate to Account Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and choose to set it up via an authenticator app (recommended) or SMS.

question: Why might a file show as 'not syncing' in Driftbox?
reference_answer: A file commonly fails to sync in Driftbox due to a poor internet connection, the file exceeding the maximum file size limit, insufficient storage space in the account, or the file being open in another program that's locking it.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Sync Troubleshooting: Files most often fail to sync due to: (1) an unstable network connection, (2) exceeding the single-file size limit for your plan, (3) the account being over its storage quota, or (4) the file being locked open by another application.

question: How long do Driftbox shared links stay active by default?
reference_answer: By default, Driftbox shared links remain active indefinitely until manually revoked, though users can optionally set an expiration date when creating the link.
context: Driftbox Help Center - File Sharing: Shared links do not expire automatically unless you set an expiration date at creation time. Links stay live until you manually disable or delete them from the Shared Links panel.

question: What happens when I exceed my Driftbox storage plan limit?
reference_answer: When you exceed your storage limit, Driftbox pauses new uploads and syncing of new or changed files, but existing files remain accessible. You'll need to free up space or upgrade your plan to resume syncing.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Storage Limits: Exceeding your plan's storage quota pauses uploads and sync for new/modified files. Previously synced files stay accessible and are not deleted. Syncing resumes automatically once you're back under the limit.

question: Can I switch from a monthly to an annual Driftbox plan in the middle of my billing cycle?
reference_answer: Yes, you can switch to an annual plan at any time from Account Settings > Billing. Driftbox will prorate your remaining monthly balance as a credit toward the new annual charge.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Billing: Plan changes, including monthly-to-annual switches, can be made anytime from Account Settings > Billing. Any unused portion of your current billing period is credited proportionally toward the new plan's cost.

question: What should I do if I think my Driftbox account was accessed without my permission?
reference_answer: Immediately change your password, enable two-factor authentication if not already active, and review the 'Active Sessions' list in Account Settings > Security to sign out any unrecognized devices.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Account Security: If you suspect unauthorized access, change your password right away, turn on two-factor authentication, and check Account Settings > Security > Active Sessions to revoke access from any device you don't recognize.

question: Why does Driftbox use more bandwidth right after I install the desktop app?
reference_answer: Right after installation, Driftbox performs an initial full sync of your entire cloud library to the new device, which temporarily uses significantly more bandwidth than normal day-to-day syncing of new changes.
context: Driftbox Help Center - Sync Troubleshooting: A newly installed desktop app performs a one-time initial sync, downloading your full library to that device. This causes a temporary spike in bandwidth usage that settles once the initial sync finishes.
